 Right Arrow OutKick How Kyle Larson turned a write-off season into his third NASCAR championship in Miami
 The Hendrick Motorsports driver became the 11th person to win consecutive titles after a turbulent regular season
 By
 Ryan Morik Fox News 
 Published
 November 12, 2026 10:00am EST Comments

 close Video Ty Gibbs reflects on Kyle Busch's NASCAR legacy 
 NASCAR driver Ty Gibbs joins 'Fox & Friends Weekend' to discuss racing a tribute car at Bristol to honor Kyle Busch. Gibbs shares the lessons he learned from his longtime role model as NASCAR rallies around Busch's family. Wife of Kyle Busch, Samantha, says returning to one of Kyle's favorite tracks will be heartbreaking, but the tribute offers a chance to keep his racing legacy alive.
 Kyle Larson is in rare company.
 The 34-year-old became the 11th person to win back-to-back NASCAR championships , winning the title in Miami on Sunday.

 "It’s really cool. The way our season went makes this one extra rewarding," Larson told OutKick in a recent interview.
 CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE 
 Kyle Larson celebrates with the trophy after winning the 2026 NASCAR Cup Series championship at Homestead-Miami Speedway in Homestead, Florida, on Nov. 8. (IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect) 
 Entering the Chase in September, Larson had not had a victory throughout a tumultuous up-and-down campaign. If he wasn't finishing in the top 10 , he was finishing in the 20s and 30s. He had 12 finishes outside the top 20 and 14 inside the top 10 .
 But when the calendar flipped, something clicked. He finished fifth at Darlington and then won the Enjoy Illinois 300 the following week. He then took second at Bristol, then won the Hollywood Casino 400 and finished second again in Las Vegas. Three weeks later, it was another checkered flag at Talladega.
 "We weren’t really that good," Larson admitted, adding that it took him and his team "months to get a grasp" on what his new car "needed."
 "By late spring, I was thinking, 'OK, we can write this season off for a championship. Let’s just try to build to be better for next year.'"
 Larson fell into the old "cliché" of patience, taking things week by week and anything else similar for any NASCAR driver.
 "But it was really true for us this year," he said.
 Kyle Larson celebrates with his family and teammates after winning the NASCAR Cup Series Championship at Homestead-Miami Speedway in Homestead, Florida, on Nov. 8, 2026. (IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect) 
 SIGN UP FOR THE DAILY OUTKICK NEWSLETTER 
 And when September hit, it was full speed ahead, no pun intended.
 "Then it snowballed. We kept getting good run after good run, which turned into a couple of wins. Suddenly, we were leading the points, and it was, 'Wow, this happened quickly.'
 "That’s what makes me most proud about this season. From start to finish, it was a lot of hard work and grinding, and all four of our Hendrick Motorsports teams coming together. It was rewarding for sure—probably one of the most rewarding championships we’ve had," the now three-time title winner said.
 Winning in this sport is rare. Even Larson said one win this season would have been nice. But this is now three times Larson has reached the mountaintop.
 Now, Larson wants to become the third person to get three in a row.
 "I think we have a great foundation as a team. We proved that this year, as we won a championship with not the fastest car. At no point in the year did we have the fastest car, but we had the best team," Larson said.
 Kyle Larson celebrates after winning the 2026 NASCAR Cup Series championship at Homestead-Miami Speedway in Homestead, Florida, on Nov. 8. (IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect)

 "I think you just carry on with what we’ve built to this point. Obviously, you want to fine-tune things and get the cars better. You fine-tune your people, but we have a really good base. You stay true to our process and see if we can three-peat."
